title: Lourdes Gurriel Jr., integral to D-Backs’ 2023 World Series run, designated for assignment
content:
With 13 games remaining in the regular season and their playoff hopes hanging by a thread, the Arizona Diamondbacks designated outfielder Lourdes Gurriel Jr. for assignment on Sunday. A key piece in Arizona’s run to the 2023 World Series, Gurriel had just returned from a right adductor strain on Sept. 7, his second injury this season and his third stint on the IL after a season-ending torn right ACL last year delayed his 2026 debut until mid-April.

“We knew that the timing was getting better, but it wasn’t where we needed it to be,” manager Torey Lovullo told reporters. “The at-bats, at times, we felt like lacked a little bit of consistency. With where we are in this point in the season, we just didn’t have time to get him to that place where he could be the Lourdes Gurriel that we remember.”

Gurriel, the younger brother of former big-leaguer Yuli Gurriel, defected from Cuba in 2016 and signed a seven-year, $22 million pact with the Toronto Blue Jays that same year. He spent the 2017 season in the minors before making his big-league debut in 2018. The outfielder was traded with catcher Gabriel Moreno to Arizona before the 2023 season in a deal that sent Daulton Varsho to Toronto.

In 2023, Gurriel hit .261/.309/.463, with a career-high 24 home runs and 35 doubles en route to his lone All-Star appearance. Arizona, which made the postseason via the wild card, manufactured a Cinderella run to the World Series, beating the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers and Philadelphia Phillies along the way before falling to the Texas Rangers in five games.

Gurriel, in his age-29 season, served as a linchpin for the Diamondbacks offense, posting a .923 OPS in the National League Division Series, a .730 OPS in the National League Championship Series and an .850 OPS in the World Series, tallying three home runs and three doubles across all four series.

Those efforts earned Gurriel a three-year, $42 million deal that offseason to keep him in Arizona. However, 2023 represented the apex of his career. He was limited to 133 games in 2024 and 129 in 2025, with his OPS declining each year.

By 2026, things bottomed out, with Gurriel struggling on all fronts and necessitating a tough decision from the Arizona front office.

“The discussion last night with Lourdes was painful for all of us,” Lovullo said. “He’s meant so much to this organization. He has carried us at times, led us to a World Series, has been a very dependable bat, a great teammate, a big influence inside of that clubhouse, and saying goodbye to that is never easy.”

The Diamondbacks could not afford to give Gurriel the necessary at-bats to get his timing back on track. At its best, Arizona’s outfield has rookie Ryan Waldschmidt in left field, Jordan Lawlar in center and Corbin Carroll in right, with Lars Nootbaar at DH. That quartet, plus the return of Tommy Troy and re-signing of Pavin Smith, made Gurriel expendable.

The club, which at one point maintained outright possession of one of the NL’s three wild-card positions, has spent the past several weeks jockeying with the San Diego Padres for the third and final postseason spot. Entering Sunday, the Diamondbacks sat 1 1/2 games back of the Padres for that third spot. Arizona does not maintain a tiebreaker over San Diego, though it will face the Padres on the road for the season’s final series.

The Diamondbacks have not reached the postseason since that 2023 run to the World Series.
